A1.justification: The PDFs describe successive versions of the same geospatial assistant, despite substantial renaming and expansion. All eight v1 pages and nine v2 pages, including equations, figures, tables, and references, support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original POI-detection results on 4,300 queries in Table 1 and image-matching accuracy/runtime measurements across filtering distances in Table 2.

after.justification: V2 retains the POI experiment and reports original venue-ranking results in Table II and spatial-understanding accuracy, object coverage, and latency results in Section IV.D.

M1.justification: The grid-based planning and bearing-based navigation procedures are retained under new names. However, v2 replaces image-to-image threshold matching with CLIP image/text place representations and XGBoost ranking using distance, heading, and popularity features. It also introduces a distilled Florence-2 spatial-understanding module and explicit orchestrator-mediated agent coordination.

E1.justification: V2 adds street-view object identification and spatial-relationship understanding, using 40,000 images for training-data generation and 400 test images. These tasks were absent from v1. The ten-city map-query coverage and Caffe Nero navigation example remain; geographic overlap between the versions' venue-evaluation data is unspecified.

E2.justification: The three POI-detection baselines remain unchanged. V2 adds distance-sorting and similarity-sorting comparisons for venue ranking in Table II. Section IV.D additionally evaluates Florence-VL 8B for accuracy, ASM v2 for object coverage, and an external-model agentic pipeline for latency.

E3.justification: V1's filtering-radius sweep measuring matching accuracy and runtime is replaced by venue-ranking evaluation with 500 training queries, 50 held-out queries, and precision/recall at ranks 1 and 3. New spatial evaluation uses 400 images, OpenAI o1 judgments, object counts, and latency measurements. The 4,300-query POI protocol is retained.

E4.justification: V2 removes the entire 100–1,000-meter filtering-radius sensitivity analysis, eliminating v1's evidence about retrieval degradation and runtime growth. It adds a worked nearest-boba reasoning case with agent traces in Figures 8–9 and a qualitative spatial-relation comparison in Figure 12. The existing navigation case is retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated evaluation runs, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's five prompts per training image describe data generation, not statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table I preserves all four POI accuracies from v1 Table 1: 39.30%, 41.46%, 42.74%, and 89.83%. The distance-sweep results disappear. New results include XGBoost precision@1 of 80.4%, spatial accuracy of 84% versus Florence-VL's 27%, approximately seven versus four objects for ASM v2, and 1.7 versus 12.4 seconds against the agentic pipeline. These are new comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: V1's explicit radius-filtered and similarity-thresholded candidate-set definitions in Section 2.3 are removed with the replacement retrieval procedure. The bearing and relative-orientation equations remain unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from three travel-lifecycle agents emphasizing disruption management to IMAIA's Maps Plus/PAISA framework emphasizing conversational maps, camera-aware grounding, and efficient spatial reasoning. V2 drops v1's 34% navigation-error reduction, 93% navigation-success, and 85% disruption-handling claims, while introducing distilled-model accuracy and speed claims.

C2.justification: V1 explains retrieval deterioration through reduced spatial locality and increasing candidate counts; this limitation discussion disappears. V2 instead interprets ranking gains as improved relevant-candidate coverage and spatial gains as benefits of task-aligned distillation over parameter scaling. It also connects richer object coverage and lower latency to scene understanding and practical deployment.

D1.justification: V2 documents CLIP feature construction, teacher and annotation models, five mining prompts per image, top-ten entity selection, over fifteen query variants, and full-parameter Florence-2-large training in Dense Region Captioning format. It also identifies NVIDIA V100 32GB evaluation hardware. Conversely, v1's proprietary/Yelp review-data provenance statement is removed. Full training hyperparameters remain unspecified.

R1.justification: V2 introduces a substantive Related Work section positioning the system against geospatial language models and spatial-reasoning approaches including ASMv2, SpatialVLM, and SpatialRGPT. It adds extensive component-model references and arguments about latency and task alignment. V1's Yelp-analysis and human-walking-path references are removed; most earlier geospatial references are retained.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, substantial introduction passages, and conclusion are rewritten. The three-agent narrative is reorganized around Maps Plus and PAISA, with dedicated related work and expanded architectural subsections. Navigation discussion is substantially condensed, and author/header information changes. This is extensive restructuring beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 reworks the system overview, adds grid-analysis, PAISA architecture, agent-trace, and spatial-answer displays, and replaces the distance-sweep table with a differently structured ranking table. Existing map and navigation examples are redisplayed with revised sizing, legends, and captions. The document adopts a different two-column template and removes v1's overlapping placeholder running headers.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves methodological specificity and empirical assessability through a documented ranking model, held-out baseline comparisons, and a detailed spatial-model training recipe with accuracy and latency evaluation. It also removes numerical navigation/disruption claims that v1 did not substantiate with corresponding experimental descriptions. The lost radius-sensitivity analysis and incomplete training, judging, and uncertainty details remain limitations, but the stronger connection between specified methods, reported protocols, and central claims constitutes a substantial overall improvement.
